abstract: In the field of relay protection in DC distribution networks, quickly and reliably identifying DC line faults has always been one of the challenges. When a fault occurs in a DC line, the current in the line will suddenly increase and flow into the fault point from both sides of the line. Based on this, this article proposes a protection method for DC zero crossing, specifically by detecting the zero crossing characteristics of the current on both sides of the line, determining whether the line has a fault, and then cutting off the line to avoid further expansion of the fault. Simultaneously analyze the impact of transition resistance and lightning on protection criteria, and propose corresponding measures. Finally, in order to further verify the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed method, a typical DC distribution network model was established based on PSCAD software, and the accuracy of the typical fault analysis and protection method criteria was set in the model. The simulation results show that the zero crossing protection method proposed in this paper for DC distribution networks can accurately identify faulty lines based on the zero crossing characteristics on both sides of the line. This method has the characteristics of simple principle and easy implementation, and can adapt well to DC distribution networks.

articleTitle: Flashover Characteristics of 500kV Insulators under Positive Short-tail Wave Impulse
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on DC Technologies and Systems (DCTS)
abstract: The $U_{50 \%}$ and volt-time characteristics of insulators are crucial models for lightning protection of transmission lines. Since negative lightning predominates in natural thunderstorms, the voltage across insulator during back flashover is characterized by the rapidly decaying positive short-tail wave. Therefore, it is necessary to further investigate the flashover characteristics of different material insulators under the various short-tail wave pulses and establish accurate flashover criteria. Experiments have provided the flashover criteria for 500 kV insulators under positive short-tail wave pulses, offering a basis for accurately assessing the lightning withstand level of transmission lines. By comparing the experimental results of glass insulators and composite insulators, the influence of material properties and altitude on flashover characteristics has been analyzed. It is found that there are significant differences in the discharge paths of insulators made from different materials, while the effect of material on the flashover characteristics is relatively small, with $U_{50} \%$ differing by only $\mathbf{2. 7 \%}$. Regarding the impact of altitude, by adopting different standards for the calibration of $U_{50 \%}$ and breakdown voltage of volt-time characteristics, it is determined that under short-tail wave conditions, the test values at high altitudes, after calibration using the g-parameter method and IEC 60071-2 standard, showed significantly reduced discrepancies compared to those from plain areas.

articleTitle: Research on the Configuration of New Energy Storage Capacity and Cost Evaluation for Large New Energy Bases
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on DC Technologies and Systems (DCTS)
abstract: This paper focuses on the demand scenarios for energy storage in the context of cross-provincial and cross-regional transmission of large-scale new energy bases. It puts forward the ideas for capacity planning regarding the supporting construction of new energy storage, and proposes an energy storage cost assessment method that takes into account the residual value and power generation benefits. Moreover, preliminary calculations have been carried out based on the existing economic and technological levels.

articleTitle: A Magnetron Method for Enhancing the Erosion Resistance of Vacuum Interrupter Contacts Using Halbach Arrays
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on DC Technologies and Systems (DCTS)
abstract: The application of an axial magnetic field (AMF) can promote the rapid transition of a vacuum arc into a diffuse mode, effectively preventing arc constriction. This method is highly effective in mitigating localized overheating and reducing material loss on the contact surface. This paper aims to investigate the effect of Halbach arrays-based AMF on the erosion resistance of contacts under high-current vacuum conditions (4 kA-16 kA). The erosion process of the contacts under the Halbach arrays-based AMF was recorded using a high-speed camera. At the conclusion of the experiment, the microscopic morphology of the contact surface was observed using an electron microscope. The surface was found to be smooth, with no significant ablation pits, and the Cr particles were fine and evenly distributed, demonstrating uniform ablation characteristics. The results indicate that the 80-110 mT AMF generated by the Halbach arrays can significantly enhance the anti-melting resistance of the contacts.

articleTitle: Research On The Calculation Of Air Clearance In The Valve Hall Of A Converter Station Under Ultra-High Altitude Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on DC Technologies and Systems (DCTS)
abstract: To ensure the reasonable and safe electrical layout for converter stations, appropriate air clearance must be determined. At high altitudes, air clearance design has a significant impact. The g parameter method which is commonly used for adjusting non-standard meteorological conditions, is applicable only when the altitude is below 2000 m. With the development of HVDC technology, many converter stations are located above 2000 m, some even over 4000 m. The national standard GB/T 42001-2022 provides additional altitude correction methods for systems above 2000 m, but detailed analysis is lacking. This paper calibrates air clearance for altitudes of $2880 \mathrm{~m}, 3000 \mathrm{~m}, 4000 \mathrm{~m}$, and 4500 m based on the g parameter method and GB/T 420012022, and compares the differences to provide a reference for high-altitude HVDC converter station design.

articleTitle: Economic Analysis of a Fractional Frequency Offshore Wind Power System Utilizing PMSG for Direct-Drive Turbines Without Terminal Converters
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on DC Technologies and Systems (DCTS)
abstract: This paper introduces the topology and working principles of a fractional frequency offshore wind power system based on permanent magnet synchronous generator for wind turbines with terminal converters. It thoroughly investigates the methods for determining the center frequency and frequency variation range on the low-frequency side of the system. An economic analysis model for the offshore wind power system is established, which includes initial investment, annual loss costs, and annual maintenance costs. Based on the developed economic analysis model and specific examples, the total present value of costs for offshore wind power systems transmitted via four different transmission methods is analyzed and compared, validating the feasibility and economic viability of the proposed topology.

Author Keywords: fractional frequency offshore wind power system

articleTitle: Unsupervised learning and expanded strategy for Multi-parameter coupling oil-immersed transformer intelligent fault diagnosis system
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on DC Technologies and Systems (DCTS)
abstract: The scarcity and imbalance of transformer fault data can result in issues such as model overfitting, reduced model representativeness, and diminished performance on test sets, thereby making it challenging to accurately assess the condition of the transformer. To address this issue, the paper investigates the similarity between the sequence of dissolved gases in transformer oil and DNA sequences. It then introduces a case augmentation method for dissolved gases in transformer oil, based on pseudo-random integration. This approach aims to provide additional data while mitigating the randomness that can lead to instability in classification accuracy. Furthermore, most current methods are unable to tackle the challenge of zero-sample identification, which involves recognizing fault conditions that are not present in the training data and for which no prior examples exist. This limitation hinders their practical application. To achieve this, the K-means++ clustering algorithm is utilized. Leveraging the characteristics of dissolved gas cases in oil, unsupervised learning and classification are performed. Additionally, a Kvalue estimation method based on the Silhouette coefficient and the Calinski-Harabaz index is proposed, which improves the efficacy and reliability of the unsupervised performance. The experiment confirmed the effectiveness of using a deep residual network (ResNet) to classify nine different transformer fault states. The results indicated that, with the same initial dataset, the pseudo-random integration method yields significantly more accurate and stable outcomes, enhancing the accuracy of transformer fault classification.

articleTitle: Exploration and Practice of Industry-Education Integration and Collaborative Education for Postgraduate Training in the Field of New Electrical Engineering
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on DC Technologies and Systems (DCTS)
abstract: Taking the electrical engineering major at South China University of Technology as an example, this paper explores a novel mechanism for joint postgraduate cultivation under the model of “industry-education integration and collaborative education”. Firstly, the curriculum system for electrical engineering is reconstructed through interdisciplinary integration and university-industry collaboration. Then, a collaborative postgraduate cultivation mechanism based on university-industry cooperation is established. Additionally, a novel mode of engineering professional certification, tailored to meet the demands of the industry, has also been designed. Finally, practical implementations demonstrate that this new mechanism has significantly improved the comprehensive quality and employment competitiveness of students, providing valuable experience and an effective exploration path for the cultivation of high-level talents in the field of energy and power.

articleTitle: Placement and Sizing Method Analysis for Distributed Renewable Energy in Distributed AC/DC Power System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on DC Technologies and Systems (DCTS)
abstract: With the increasing demand and proportion of distributed Renewable Energy (DRE) connected to the distributed AC/DC Power System, the issue of appropriate placement and sizing for distribution network evaluation has gained significant prominence. Proper placement of DRE in distributed AC/DC power system can mitigate power loss to enhance operation reliability. Currently, most placement indicators primarily focus on steady-state capabilities, such as active power loss and voltage distribution. However, the improved transient capacity of the distributed AC/DC power system is also an indicator that cannot be ignored. This paper presents analysis of the current mainstream DRE placement method that developed various types of indicators, along with a thorough examination of existing distributed AC/DC power system vulnerability node selection indices. It highlights the shortcomings of existing placement indicators and their inherent connection with vulnerability analysis in terms of both steady-state and transient placement. Simulation results demonstrate that the integration of DRE under this model can reduce node vulnerability, enhance recovery capabilities, and offer a novel perspective of DRE placement in distributed AC/DC power system.

articleTitle: High-frequency modelling and optimal design of common-mode inductors for EMI suppression of valve cooling system sensors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on DC Technologies and Systems (DCTS)
abstract: Common mode filters play a crucial role in ensuring the reliability of sensors in valve cooling systems. Accurate modeling of common mode inductors under high-frequency operating conditions can help better design and optimize filters. This article points out the limitations of commonly used analytical models and proposes a more comprehensive and accurate analytical model that comprehensively considers material factors, the influence of time-varying electromagnetic fields, and the geometric characteristics of common mode inductors to solve the errors caused by traditional analytical models. In addition, this article also provides a detailed explanation of the physical significance behind the proposed model. This article compares two methods and validates the proposed method through simulations and experiments in four different scenarios. Finally, this article proposes a high-frequency optimization design method for common mode inductors.

articleTitle: Voltage Disturbance Observation Method Based on Dual Active Bridge Converter Loss Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on DC Technologies and Systems (DCTS)
abstract: The Dual Active Bridge (DAB) DC-DC converter has garnered widespread attention in fields such as electric vehicle power supplies, charging piles, and smart grids due to its advantages of bidirectional energy flow, high power density, ease of implementing soft-switching characteristics, and high efficiency. Research on DAB mainly focuses on two aspects: modulation methods and optimized control. By adjusting operational parameters such as the DAB’s return power, effective value of inductor current, and current stress, the goals of reducing losses and improving efficiency are achieved. However, due to model errors and nonlinear characteristics, the theoretically calculated optimal operating mode may deviate from the actual situation, necessitating the use of a closed-loop mechanism for correction. This paper directly addresses the control object of power loss in DAB converters composed of Gallium Nitride (GaN), proposing a loss model that is more direct and concise compared to traditional loss models. Through simulation verification, the input voltage value is locked using the voltage disturbance observation method, and the significance and value of the loss model are demonstrated.

articleTitle: Transformer Anomaly Detection Using Deep Belief Network with Dynamic Adaptive Knowledge Transfer and Interval Type-2 Fuzzy Set for Uncertain Parameters
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on DC Technologies and Systems (DCTS)
abstract: Power transformers are key and expensive components in power systems. Precise evaluation of the transformer state is critically essential. This article presents a transformer fault diagnosis technique utilizing a deep belief network (DBN) enhanced with dynamic adaptive knowledge transfer (DAKT) and interval type 2 uncertain parameter fuzzy set (IT2F) structure. Firstly, in accordance with the compaction aspects of chaotic phase space and the Lyapunov index in chaos theory as quantitative judgment, the optimal analysis data selection method is obtained, which reduces invalid data and improves calculation accuracy. Subsequently, a neuro-symbolic framework is introduced to elucidate the operational dynamics of the profound architecture, and a novel sparse deep belief network leveraging adaptive knowledge transition is constructed utilizing the knowledge integration technique of rule amalgamation and elimination. This network possesses a more sparse topology and superior learning efficacy. Secondly, a new enhanced deep learning algorithm-interval type 2 uncertain parameter fuzzy set is introduced the parameters and offsets of the deep belief network, which can better handle the uncertainty between the input data and model parameters. Strengthen the robustness and generalization capability of the model. Comparative analysis with shallow machine learning methods and deep learning methods shows that the average recognition rate of the proposed DAKT-IT2F-DBN method is $97.43 \%$, with good robustness and performance exceeding other fault diagnosis methods.

Author Keywords: Interval type 2 uncertain parameter fuzzy set

articleTitle: Short Circuit Currents Constrained Switching Optimization Enhancing Flexibility of Urban Power Grid with Energy Storage System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on DC Technologies and Systems (DCTS)
abstract: In the context of increasingly excessive short-circuit current in urban power grids, disconnecting transmission lines can improve the flexibility of system operation while reducing short-circuit current. However, this also reduces transmission capacity, leading to more severe line overloads, increased operational costs, and limitations on the integration of clean energy and loads. Additionally, the extensive access of new energy sources, further elevates the level of short-circuit current, resulting in serious issues of short-circuit current exceeding limits and transmission line overloads in urban power grids. To fill this gap, a coordinated optimization strategy for switching optimization and ES scheduling considering SCC constraint based on model predictive control (MPC) is proposed in this paper. Numerical results show that the proposed strategy can maximize the flexibility of UPGs while reducing the hazards of SCC and mitigating the transmission congestion.

articleTitle: Seismic performance analysis of DC transmission tower-line system of unequal height
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on DC Technologies and Systems (DCTS)
abstract: To explore the influence of unequal leg length combinations on the seismic performance of DC transmission towers, transmission tower models with different leg heights were established for seismic response analysis, Based on incremental dynamic analysis (IDA) method and the failure determination criteria, the dynamic stability performance of unequal tower-wire system under seismic action for $0,3,6$, and 9 m height difference was analyzed. Results indicate that the design of long and short legs makes the vibration mode of transmission tower change, and the joint of short leg and tower body with main material stress increase. The vibration phenomenon of shifting the equilibrium position occurs in the near unstable state, the impact of the unbalanced tension in the conductor of the key components damage aggravated leading to instability damage. Finally, As the height gap increases, the modal effect manifests the stress increase is particularly clear, the unequal tower leg design in the direction of the conductor should be avoided as much as possible in the construction of the project.

articleTitle: Converter Transformer fault diagnosis method based on double-weighted loss function and DT-Lightgbm-Gcforest
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on DC Technologies and Systems (DCTS)
abstract: A converter transformer fault diagnosis method based on double-weighted loss function and DT-Lightgbm-Gcforest is proposed to improve the effect of converter transformer fault diagnosis under the unbalanced sample data. Aiming at unbalanced fault samples and the difficulty of diagnosing complex categories, the category sample distribution and the interpretation degree of the binary Logistic model are employed to calculate the category balance weight and interpretive quantitative weights for different fault categories, and the multi-category cross-entropy loss function is constructed. Then, since the ensemble learning parameters have a large dimension and are difficult to optimize, the tree-structured parzen estimator (TPE) algorithm is employed to optimize parameters of the Light Gradient Boosting Machine (Lightgbm) and Multi-Grained Cascade Forest composed of multiple Lightgbm, dual-stage TPE optimized Lightgbm-Gcforest is established as the final fault diagnosis model. Finally, the double-weighted cross-entropy is adopted as a loss function to perform the model’s training and fault diagnosis. Simulation results indicate that the overall accuracy of the proposed method is 94.94%, which is 5.05% higher than that without weighting the cross-entropy loss function and 2.81% higher than that before using the TPE optimization algorithm, demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Flexible Retrofit Planning for Distribution Networks in Urban High-density Load Areas
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on DC Technologies and Systems (DCTS)
abstract: The increasing power demand and massive access of clean energy sources have put considerable pressure on the operation of distribution networks, especially in high-density load areas. DC distribution technology provides solutions for upgrading urban grids. In this context, this paper proposes a flexible retrofit planning model for distribution networks considering photovoltaic integration. The scheme coordinates the planning of DC lines and energy storage systems (ESSs) to mitigate local photovoltaic overflow and overload problems. The proposed model is transformed into a Mixed-Integer SecondOrder Cone Programming (MISOCP) formulation and validated through the case study based on a modified system in Zhuhai. The results demonstrate that the flexible retrofit scheme significantly enhances the economic efficiency and reliability of distribution networks.

articleTitle: Research on the carbon reduction scheme of green buildings based on DC power supply technology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on DC Technologies and Systems (DCTS)
abstract: In response to the lack of systematic analysis methods for complex power flow, system losses and carbon emissions in green building direct current (DC) power supply systems including photovoltaics, energy storages and charging piles, which has led to limited promotion of DC system applications, this paper conducts an analysis on energy consumption, carbon emissions and economy for green buildings as well as the research on carbon reduction scheme. It proposes a method for calculating system energy consumption and carbon emission coefficients and establishes the energy consumption minimum optimization model and economic optimal model. The influence of voltage level, new energy access ratio and other factors on energy efficiency and carbon emissions are analyzed. The price of carbon emissions, electric energy and green electricity are considered in economic analysis. The study conducted a comprehensive analysis of energy efficiency, carbon emissions, and economic factors in an office building located in Zhuhai, China.

articleTitle: Multi-Objective Optimal Design of High Power, High Frequency, High Voltage Transformer Considering Insulation for DC distribution Grid
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on DC Technologies and Systems (DCTS)
abstract: As DC distribution networks demonstrate widespread application potential in areas such as distributed generation and urban microgrids, high-power dc transformers are becoming more and more important. It is also called dc energy router, and offers various the functions such as voltage regulation, power flow control, isolation, etc. The core component of the dc energy router, high-frequency transformers, has become increasingly crucial. This paper presents a multi-objective optimization design scheme considering high insulation standards for high-frequency transformers. It is a $750 \mathrm{~V} / 50 \mathrm{kVA}$ transformer with a withstand voltage of 35 kV. The adoption of a double-layer insulation structure enhances insulation reliability, and an optimized selection method for internal insulation copper foil strips is presented. Based on the non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm, a multi-objective optimization is conducted, comprehensively considering transformer efficiency, power density, and leakage inductance, to optimize the design of the windings and magnetic core. Finally, the effectiveness of the design scheme is verified.
